summary: Crostini with young pecorino, grilled figs and arugula-mint pesto: baguette slices toasted about 15 minutes at 350°F, topped with soft young pecorino, blowtorched or broiled fig quarters and a pesto of baby arugula, mint, olive oil and Parmigiano; makes 12.
glance: 12 thin slices of baguette cut on the bias, brushed with olive oil, 350°F about 15 minutes
9 fresh figs, quartered and grilled, torched or broiled
2 cups baby arugula, 1/4 cup mint, 6 tablespoons olive oil, garlic, Parmigiano
faq: What is young pecorino?

Pecorino is the name for the entire family of Italian sheep's milk cheeses. If you only know pecorino romano, a hard grating cheese, seek out soft young pecorinos, which you'll find at Whole Foods or any good cheesemonger.
How do I grill the figs?

The author uses a blowtorch for small grilling tasks like this. If you don't have one or aren't comfortable with it, run them under a broiler, or use a charcoal grill for even better flavor. Brush the quartered figs with olive oil and cook until the cut surfaces are well browned.
How thick should the pesto be?
A fairly uniform but not completely pureed paste, adding more oil if needed so it is neither so thick that it stands up by itself nor as thin as a sauce.
Why add mint to arugula pesto?
The author thought a bit of fresh mint might improve the pesto from his cookbook's potato and green bean salad, and says it makes a huge difference.
Can I add pine nuts?
Yes, you certainly can; the author left out toasted pine nuts because they are poison in his house.
How do I assemble each crostini?
Put a piece of pecorino on each toast, top with 3 fig quarters mashed gently with a fork so they lie flat and hold the pesto, then spoon on pesto and finish with flaky salt and black pepper.

summary: Fava beans, potatoes and saffron rice: canned round fava beans rinsed and simmered with lemon, crispy fried potatoes with garlic and cumin, and saffron basmati rice, topped with feta, dill and mint; serves 4 as a main course.
glance: one 28-ounce or two 15-ounce cans, rinsed and simmered with lemon (a few minutes to half an hour)
1 1/2 cups basmati cooked with saffron water
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you omit the feta
faq: What is foul?

"Fool" is the word for fava beans throughout the Middle East and North Africa, as in foul mudammas. Fresh and dried favas are radically different: fresh are mild and sweet, something like a cross between a baby pea and a lima bean, and a royal pain to peel.
Which fava beans do I use?
The dish uses dried-style favas from a can: a smaller, rounder variety than the lima-shaped fresh ones. Canned are available at any good Middle Eastern market, or buy dried and boil them yourself.
How do I prepare canned favas?
Rinse thoroughly, then simmer a bit with a little lemon juice to optimize the flavor and ensure tenderness: just a few minutes if already tender, up to half an hour if a little tough.
Can I serve potatoes with rice?
The author notes many Americans feel you shouldn't serve both because they're starches, but it's common practice in much of the world, like aloo gobi with rice, and delicious.
How do I infuse the rice with saffron?
Crumble a pinch of saffron over 1/4 cup of hot water, let sit 5 minutes, and include the saffron water as part of the regular water for your basmati.
Is this a traditional Persian dish?
It seemed Persian to the author, but he doesn't know if it's traditional and invites Persian readers to comment.

summary: Gobi masala cauliflower curry: mustard seeds, onion, garlic, ginger and a spice mixture with turmeric, cumin, cinnamon, cayenne and asafoetida, then a large cauliflower cooked covered with 1/4 cup of water for about 15 minutes until tender but not mush; neither saucy nor dry, serves 4.
glance: 4 as part of an Indian meal
about 15 minutes covered, until completely tender but not falling apart
turmeric, cumin, cinnamon, cayenne, asafoetida; garam masala to finish
Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free (check the asafoetida)
yield: 4 as part of an Indian meal
faq: What is asafoetida?

Also called hing, the ground-up gum from a particular plant rhizome. It is pungent with a flavor somewhat akin to aged garlic, used in small quantities to add savor to curries and reputed to aid digestion.
How do I keep the cauliflower from turning to mush?

Pay close attention toward the end of cooking: you want it thoroughly tender but not breaking down. Make the florets as evenly sized as possible and add a bit more water only if needed for a very small amount of sauciness.
Can I use other vegetables?
Yes, any vegetable that will hold its shape and not give up too much water, such as beets or turnips. For firmer vegetables, parboil or microwave first to reduce the final cooking time.
Why add the cauliflower right after the spices?
Dump the spice mixture into the onions, stir quickly and immediately add the cauliflower to avoid burning the spices.
What is tempering?
Optionally frying more mustard seeds and cumin seeds in a little more oil for about 20 seconds and drizzling over the finished dish for extra flavor; you can play with which spices you use.
What do I serve it with?
Basmati rice, dal, raita, and tamarind chutney and/or Indian pickles for a satisfying feast.

summary: Crispy, garlicky smashed potatoes with gremolata: 5 pounds of golf-ball-sized potatoes boiled 5 minutes, baked until fork tender, smashed, topped with a whole head of minced garlic cooked in 1/2 cup olive oil and roasted at 500°F for at least 20 minutes until crispy, then finished with parsley-lemon gremolata; serves 6.
glance: 5 pounds small waxy, boiled 5 minutes, baked at 450°F, smashed
a whole head, finely minced, sauteed 2 minutes in 1/2 cup olive oil
500°F for at least 20 minutes, until the skins are crispy in many spots
faq: How much garlic do I need?

A whole head of fresh garlic, finely minced (not crushed), with plenty of good olive oil. The author says you need the nerve to use that much, and the patience to roast the potatoes until the skins crisp up.
How do I keep the garlic from burning?
Check the oven frequently. Saute the minced garlic in the oil only 2 minutes first, spoon it and the oil evenly over the potatoes, and gather all the crispy garlic bits when serving.
How do I smash the potatoes?
After boiling 5 minutes and baking until fork tender, smash each fairly aggressively so it flattens out and develops big cracks but doesn't totally mash; the bottom of a coffee mug works well.
What is gremolata?

A simple condiment of finely minced parsley, lemon zest and usually garlic, traditionally served with osso bucco. Here it omits the garlic, and the heat from the potatoes makes it give off a heady, appetizing aroma.
Where does the idea come from?
Tom Douglas serves something similar as a side at his Greek-inspired restaurant Lola; the gremolata is the author's twist.

summary: Potato and fennel gratin: boiled Yukon gold slices and blanched fennel layered with a thickened thyme-nutmeg cream sauce, topped with garlicky toasted homemade breadcrumbs and baked at 375°F about 20 minutes until bubbling; serves 4-6.
glance: 375°F for about 20 minutes, until bubbling hot
2 cups heavy cream simmered until nearly as thick as gravy, with thyme, nutmeg and lemon zest
2 cups garlicky homemade breadcrumbs, toasted until golden
faq: Why homemade breadcrumbs?

The author says garlicky homemade breadcrumbs make all of the difference. He saves every stale bit of artisan bread and grinds it; if he doesn't use them right away they freeze beautifully, so make a larger batch, and experiment with how finely you grind them.
How thick should the cream sauce be?
Thick enough to coat the back of a spoon rather well, almost as thick as gravy, because it won't have time to thicken much more in the oven.
How do I prepare the potatoes and fennel?
Boil the fennel slices 3 minutes, then rinse to cool. Boil the potatoes until tender, cool them, and slice 1/4 inch thick; don't slice them while boiling hot or they fall apart.
How do I assemble it?
Layer overlapping potatoes in a buttered 9x11 casserole, add half the fennel and half the cream sauce, repeat with another layer, and cover the top with breadcrumbs.
What do I serve with it?
A bowl of minestrone or black-bean soup and a simple salad with a mustardy vinaigrette.

summary: Savory Dutch baby with caramelized-soft onions and aged Gouda: a blender batter of 5 eggs, milk and flour mixed with onions, 1 cup of grated aged Gouda and herbes de Provence, poured into a sizzling buttered 12-inch cast-iron skillet and baked about 18 minutes at 425°F; serves 3 to 5.
glance: 425°F for about 18 minutes, until puffed and golden brown
well-seasoned 12-inch cast iron with 6 tablespoons butter heated first
faq: What is a savory Dutch baby?

A savory version of a puffed oven pancake that becomes like a very light, custardy quiche. Serve it for lunch or brunch with a green salad (apples!), or cut it into squares as an appetizer. With the cheese it won't puff as much as a normal Dutch baby.
What is aged Gouda?

Not the stuff in red wax: aged Gouda has an intense caramel or butterscotch flavor, and in the most-aged varieties is rather crystalline like parmigiano reggiano. Find it at a good cheesemonger; Trader Joe's carries a decent mid-grade one.
What is herbes de Provence?

Generally a mixture of thyme, basil, savory, fennel and a tiny bit of lavender, sometimes other herbs. Without a packet, use as many of those herbs as you have, lively and not old; or 2 tablespoons of fresh herbs. Use only a pinch of lavender or it will taste like soap.
How do I get the skillet right?
Put 6 tablespoons of butter in the skillet and heat it in the oven; when sizzling, pull it out and swirl or brush to coat, pour in the batter and return it to the oven.
How do I finish it?
Carefully remove from the oven, pat off any excess butter on top with a paper towel, and garnish with smoked paprika.

summary: Kouftikes de prasa sandwiches, a Sephardic leek patty recipe from the Herbivoracious cookbook: sauteed leeks bound with eggs and breadcrumbs, fried about 3 minutes per side, served in pita with spicy preserved lemon and harissa red cabbage, cucumber, yogurt, sumac and mint; serves 4.
glance: marinate at least 2 hours, or overnight
1/4 cup each, about 4 inches wide, fried about 3 minutes per side
faq: What is a kofta?

All over the Middle East and even in India, a little meatball or patty. There are a few vegetarian versions, like these Sephardic kouftikes de prasa, made of leeks bound together with breadcrumbs and eggs.
How do I prepare the leeks?

Cut the white and light green parts in half lengthwise, then into 1/4-inch half-circles, wash in 3 changes of water and dry thoroughly (a salad spinner works well), then saute in olive oil about 5 minutes until tender and starting to shrivel.
How do I shape and fry the patties?

Mix the leeks with the salt, eggs, breadcrumbs, cumin, Aleppo pepper or cayenne and cinnamon, drop the batter into 1/8 inch of oil with a quarter-cup measure and smooth each into a 4-inch circle. Make 8 in two batches, golden brown about 3 minutes per side.
Can I make the spicy cabbage ahead?
Yes: toss it together and refrigerate at least two hours or overnight, then bring to room temperature. In a pinch, use plain shredded lettuce and serve hot sauce on the side.
How do I build the sandwich?

Put two patties on a toasted pita, top with spicy cabbage, 5 cucumber slices and 2 tablespoons of Greek yogurt or labneh, then sumac and torn mint. This turns them from an appetizer into an entree with street food flair.

summary: Savory bread pudding with morels and beet greens: torn pain au levain tossed gently with sauteed morels, onion, garlic and squeezed-dry beet greens and a rosemary-nutmeg custard, rested 20 minutes and baked at 375°F for 45-55 minutes until about 180°F inside; serves 4.
glance: 4 as a big side dish or light main course
375°F for 45-55 minutes, to an internal temperature of about 180°F
let stand 20 minutes before baking; cool at least 15 minutes after
7 ounces (3 big thick slices) pain au levain or similar, torn
yield: 4 as a big side dish or light main course
faq: How is savory bread pudding different from stuffing?
There isn't much difference except that bread pudding is bound with eggs. Tom Douglas has done corn and mushroom bread puddings for years at Etta's and Palace Kitchen in Seattle.
How do I keep it light?

Add the richness of the custard without crushing the lightness of the bread: tear the bread instead of cutting uniform cubes to create airspace, use a hearty bread like pain au levain, and most important, toss the bread only very gently with the egg mixture, no squeezing.
Can I use other mushrooms?

Chanterelles or cultivated oyster mushrooms work if you cook them long enough to develop flavor, or a few ounces of black truffle. Soak and rinse morels well; if using other mushrooms just wipe them clean.
Can I use other greens?
Yes, any leafy green, but be sure to squeeze the water out so it doesn't sog up your bread. Here, the beet greens are boiled about 10 minutes, cooled and squeezed.
How do I know it's done?
When it reaches an internal temperature of about 180°F, checked in several places. It will still seem a bit soft but not liquid anywhere. Don't overcook or the eggs turn rubbery and leach water.
How do I cook the morels?
Saute in butter with a big pinch of salt: all the water comes out and evaporates, then they start browning, about 10 minutes total.

summary: Kimchi jigae with shiitake and daikon: chopped vegetarian kimchi, kochujang and miso softened with daikon, shiitake and onion, simmered 15 minutes in water and soy sauce, then simmered 5 more with tofu cubes; vegan, serves 4 in 35 minutes.
glance: 15 minutes, then 5 more minutes with the tofu
2 cups chopped vegetarian kimchi, 2 tablespoons kochujang, 2 tablespoons red miso
faq: What is kimchi jigae?
Classic Korean home cooking simple enough for a weeknight dinner. The body of the stew comes from chopped kimchi, spiked with chile paste (kochujang, also spelled gochujang) and miso.
Why add daikon?
Daikon is delicious in salads and pickles but heat brings out a sweet, tender side that is easy to like. Cut 2 cups of 1/4-inch half moons.
How spicy is it?
Depending on your kimchi it may already be quite spicy; if you want more heat, add more kimchi, kochujang, or powdered chili pepper (kochugaru) or chili flakes.
Can I change the ingredients?
Yes, adapt the stew to just about any ingredients you have on hand. This version uses daikon, shiitake caps and tofu.
What do I serve with it?
Rice and more kimchi for a simple meal, or a collection of Korean side dishes (banchan) for a full feast.
What if the kochujang and miso stay in lumps?
They start as big blobs but after a few minutes of cooking they soften and dissolve.

summary: Ilan Hall's Top Chef fideos adapted to be vegetarian, with a review of Top Chef: The Cookbook: thin noodles broken and toasted deep brown in the oven, cooked in garlic oil and wine, mixed with saffron cream, cauliflower and broccoli and broiled; serves 4 as an entree, or 6-8 as a side.
glance: 4 as an entree (or 6-8 as a side)
fideos broken into 3-inch pieces, 375°F for 8 to 10 minutes until dark golden
covered about 4 minutes, adding wine or water until al dente, then broil 2-4 minutes
2.5 cups each of cauliflower and broccoli florets
faq: What are fideos?

Simply thin noodles, broken into short lengths and toasted to a deep brown in the oven before cooking directly in a sauce. The toasting adds a whole layer of flavor, here bolstered with cream, white wine and loads of garlic.
Where does this recipe come from?

Ilan Hall, winner of Top Chef season 2 and a former line cook at New York's Casa Mono, made fideos with clams, cauliflower and broccoli in week 11. The recipe is from Top Chef: The Cookbook, adapted here to be clamless.
Is the Top Chef cookbook good?

The author calls it a very solid cookbook with incredible recipes, plus features on the contestants, hosts and judges, making-of info for each season and funny stuff, with great graphic design, and recommends it as a gift for fans of the show.
What if the noodles are still crunchy?
The author's were still crunchy after the last step: add more wine or water, cover the pan and keep checking every minute until al dente.
Why add more vegetables?

The author added a lot more cauliflower and broccoli than the original (2.5 cups each instead of 1), because they're succulent and tasty. The dish is rich, so it may work even better as a side for 6-8.
